--- title: "Data" subtitle: "Where the shade and heat maps come from, and who we follow home." jupyter: python3 --- ## Sources All inputs are public. | Layer | Source | Used for | | --- | --- | --- | | Airborne LiDAR, March 2022 | City of Philadelphia (NOAA Digital Coast, PASDA) | ground, building and tree heights at 1 m | | Building footprints | City of Philadelphia | building outlines | | Land cover 2018 | PASDA | tree canopy | | Canopy height (CHMv2) | Meta / WRI | trees just outside the city | | Pedestrian network | DVRPC | sidewalks and crosswalks | | OpenStreetMap | OSM contributors | bridges, covered walkways, campus footways in University City | | Building entrances and indoor passages | mapped for this project, 41 buildings in University City | walks through buildings | | Transit | SEPTA, fall 2026 timetable | stations and frequent bus or trolley stops | | Properties | City of Philadelphia (OPA) | homes, where walks end | | Hourly weather | ERA5 (ECMWF), via Open-Meteo | weather for the heat model | | Heat model | SOLWEIG 2022a (solweig-gpu 2.0.0) | felt temperature (UTCI) at 1 m | | Surface temperature, air temperature | USGS Landsat 8; NOAA ACIS | heat figures on the Story page | ## Heights and shade ::: {.stat-row}
7,237 km
sidewalks and crossings
3.6 M
points checked for shade, every 2 m
24
hours modelled: 8:00–19:00 on two days
::: Bridges and elevated rail cast shadows as well as buildings and trees. Trees cover 17% of the city (median height 15 m). Covered walkways (4.2 km) are always in shade. ::: {#57cf6724 .cell .figure-light execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ![University City in the height model: buildings with LiDAR heights (blue) or recorded heights (pink), bridges and other structures (orange) and trees (green).](data_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-1.jpeg){} ::: ::: ## The heat model Shade says where the sun is blocked, not how hot a sidewalk feels. SOLWEIG takes the same heights and the weather and computes the radiation a standing person receives from the sun, the sky, walls and the ground. From it comes the **UTCI**, how hot it feels in °C. Above 38 °C is *very strong* heat stress, above 46 °C *extreme*. The heat model uses the weather of two hot, sunny days in 2025: **June 24**, during a heat wave, and **July 29**. | Day | Air temperature, 15:00 | Humidity, 15:00 | Wind, 15:00 | Peak solar radiation | Daily maximum | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | June 24, 2025 | 38.5 °C | 32% | 2.8 m/s | 936 W/m² | 38.8 °C | | July 29, 2025 | 36.1 °C | 43% | 1.8 m/s | 914 W/m² | 36.1 °C | One ERA5 cell covers the whole city, so air temperature and wind are the same everywhere; the heat map varies with sun, shade, walls and ground. ## Whose walks Each walk starts at a rapid-transit station (Regional Rail, the L and B subway lines, and the T trolley tunnel) or at a bus or trolley stop with at least 6 departures an hour on one route in one direction between 15:00 and 19:00, and ends at a home within 1.2 km on foot: 431,114 walks. The other 91,659 homes (17.5%), mostly in the Northeast and Roxborough, have no frequent stop that close. ::: {#0252b821 .cell .figure-light execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ![Homes without a frequent stop within 1.2 km (red).](data_files/figure-html/cell-9-output-1.jpeg){width=640} ::: ::: ## Known gaps - Campus and park paths are missing outside University City, so cooler options there are understated. - Milder or cloudy days are not modelled. - Trees come from leaf-off LiDAR and 2018 land cover, and let a fixed 3% of the sun through.
